Class 2 · Chapter 2 of 9

Add, subtract and make equal groups

Add and take away with swaps, count equal groups and find the missing part.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Hundreds, tens and ones. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can add and subtract in a story.
  • I can count equal groups.
  • I can find a missing digit or amount.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Add with a swap

38 + 27: add the ones first. 8 + 7 = 15 ones.

15 ones is too many. Swap 10 ones for 1 ten. Then 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 tens, so the answer is 65.

Screen 2 of 5

Take away with a swap

52 − 27: you cannot take 7 ones from 2 ones.

Swap 1 ten for 10 ones. Now 52 is 4 tens and 12 ones. Take away 2 tens and 7 ones: 25 left.

Screen 3 of 5

Equal groups

3 plates with 4 biscuits on each plate.

Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12. So 3 groups of 4 make 12.

Screen 4 of 5

Jump on a number line

Each jump is one group of 4.

Three jumps of 4 start at 0 and land on 12.

Screen 5 of 5

Find the missing part

The whole is 73. One part is 45. The other part is hiding.

Take away to find it: 73 − 45 = 28.

Words to know
swap
Trade 10 ones for 1 ten, or 1 ten for 10 ones. The amount stays the same.
equal groups
Groups with the same number of things in each.
array
Things in neat rows and columns, so equal groups are easy to count.

2 Try it

Now you do it. Move the pieces, then press Check my answer.

Activity 1

Show 38 + 27. It starts as 5 tens and 15 ones. Swap until the ones are fewer than 10.

Chapter passed. Next: Find number and picture rules

For parents

What your child learns

Equalising means sharing so both groups match. If one tray has 6 more than the other, the giver gives half of the difference. Equal jumps on a line split the distance evenly.

A common slip

Children may give the whole difference instead of half. Move one at a time and compare after each. For jumps, divide the distance by the number of jumps.

5-minute home activity: Make them equal

  1. Put 9 counters on one plate and 3 on another.
  2. Move one at a time from the larger to the smaller.
  3. Stop when both plates match and count what moved.
  4. Draw 3 equal jumps from 20 to 35 and find one jump.
